title: The Lighter Brief
overview: A fairly mixed day! Congress spent Tuesday evening voting on a proposed impeachment, Charlotte rolled out new street-vending rules, and the FDA added a rare eye-risk warning to popular GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic. On the lighter side, Method Man plays a rapper fighting AI copycats on TV, and Lil Yachty is bringing wrestling style to holiday shopping.

stories.headline: House Republicans set aside Hegseth impeachment, for now
stories.summary: The House voted Tuesday evening to send a measure to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth back to committee, which effectively blocks it for now. The articles were filed by Republican Rep. Thomas Massie, who accused Hegseth of abusing his power and failing to protect civilians. Republican leaders had been bracing for possible defections, so the vote counts as a win for them and the administration. Axios notes Democrats are expected to raise the issue again when they take control of both chambers in January.
key_facts: The vote referred the impeachment measure back to committee instead of moving it forward.
Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) filed the articles of impeachment.
Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.) said a traffic incident and police escort kept her and other lawmakers from reaching the Capitol in time to vote.
Democrats take majorities in the House and Senate in January.
stories.why: It shows where things stand on a high-profile oversight fight that will likely come back once the new Congress is seated.

stories.headline: Jamaica's opposition presses PM over UN Cuba vote
stories.summary: Opposition MP Anthony Hylton wants his censure motion against the government put back on Parliament's agenda after debate on it was cut short on November 3. He is also asking Prime Minister Andrew Holness to explain in Parliament why Jamaica abstained in the UN vote on lifting the US embargo on Cuba. Hylton argues that Parliament passed a Cuba resolution on October 27 believing Jamaica's position hadn't changed, only for Jamaica to abstain the next day.
key_facts: Jamaica abstained in the UN vote on October 28.
Leader of Government Business Floyd Green moved to close the censure debate under Standing Order 38, and the 'ayes' prevailed.
Hylton says the abstention was a Cabinet decision, so Cabinet answers to Parliament collectively.
disputed: The opposition says it believes the abstention decision was sent to Jamaica's UN mission before or during the House debate. That is the opposition's claim and has not been confirmed in this article.
stories.why: It raises the question of how much Parliament should be told about foreign-policy shifts before it votes on related resolutions.

stories.headline: Trinidad ruling gives hope to Jamaica buggery-law challenge
stories.summary: The Privy Council, the final appeals court for Trinidad and Tobago, ruled that the island's anti-buggery laws can't be used to criminalise private, consensual relations between adult men. That ends an 11-year legal fight led by Jason Jones. Activist and lawyer Maurice Tomlinson says the ruling will be 'highly persuasive' for his own challenge to Jamaica's laws, which the same court is due to hear next year.
key_facts: Jason Jones, 62, first won in Trinidad's High Court in 2018, but that win was overturned on appeal before this final ruling.
Tomlinson has been challenging Jamaica's laws since 2015.
Jamaica's laws date to the 1864 Offences Against the Person Act (sections 76, 77 and 79).
Jamaica's constitution has a 'savings law' clause that shields older laws from challenge, which Tomlinson plans to argue against.
stories.why: A ruling from a court shared by several Caribbean countries could shape how similar laws are handled across the region.

links.title: BUGGERY LAW SHOWDOWN - Tomlinson banking on Trinidad ruling to bolster similar legal challenge for Jamaica next year

stories.headline: CMU fraud trial: witness says third-party payments were routine
stories.summary: In the ongoing fraud trial over Caribbean Maritime University spending, a former treasurer was questioned about payments to JLP councillor Kim Brown Lawrence. He agreed she was a third-party payee under contracts between CMU and consultancy firm Optimum Customer Services Consultancy, and that none of the documents shown contained payment instructions from her. He also said all 14 to 15 meal contractors on a youth programme were paid the same way.
key_facts: More than 60 documents, including cheque vouchers, have been admitted into evidence.
The prosecution alleges former CMU President Fritz Pinnock authorised millions in payments to several people for student meals.
The payments relate to the CAP-YES youth employment programme.
disputed: The payments are alleged to be fraudulent. The trial is ongoing and no verdict has been reached.
stories.why: It's a closely watched case about how public university money was handled.

stories.headline: Charlotte's new street-vending rules are in effect
stories.summary: As of Monday, street vending on Charlotte's streets and sidewalks is allowed only in pre-approved areas, which for now are mostly in Uptown. The City Council also dropped criminal penalties for vending violations and replaced them with civil fines. Council members say the goal is to give vendors structure, not to shut them down. Some members worry the fines won't deter repeat violators.
key_facts: Violations carry civil fines of up to $500 each and could lead to losing a vending license.
Approved spots are designated by Center City Partners.
There's no clear timeline yet for adding vending zones outside Uptown.
CMPD is building a system to track violations.
stories.why: If you sell or shop from street vendors in Charlotte, where they can set up has changed.

stories.headline: Offset says he and Quavo are still healing, together
stories.summary: Offset told DJ Whoo Kid on Shade 45 that he and Quavo had been talking privately well before they were seen together at Quavo's September album celebration. He said they are still grieving Takeoff and keeping much of that process private. The two are making music together again, and Quavo has talked about new Migos music and a Takeoff project.
key_facts: Offset appears on 'Away' from Quavo's album QRÖMELIFE, released October 2.
Pharrell Williams executive produced QRÖMELIFE.
Quavo says future Migos work should honor Takeoff and benefit his estate.
disputed: Plans for new Migos music and a Takeoff project have been discussed but not formally announced with dates.
stories.why: It's a sweet sign of family and bandmates finding their way back to each other after a hard loss.

links.title: Offset Says He And Quavo Still Need Time To Heal

stories.headline: Method Man takes on AI copycats on CBS's 'Cupertino'
stories.summary: Wu-Tang Clan's Method Man guest-stars on the CBS legal drama Cupertino as YUNGWOOD, a veteran rapper whose streaming income drops when an AI studio starts copying his music. The show's attorneys take the studio to court, and the case also puts lead lawyer Michael across the courtroom from his own father.
key_facts: The episode airs Thursday, November 12, at 10 p.m. ET/PT on CBS.
It streams live on Paramount+ Premium, and on demand the next day for Paramount+ Essential subscribers.
Mike Colter and Rachel Keller star in the series.
stories.why: It's a fun, timely TV plot about AI and music, with a familiar face in the lead.

links.title: Method Man Takes AI Copycats To Court In New CBS Role

stories.headline: Lil Yachty fronts a Lids holiday campaign with a WWE twist
stories.summary: Lil Yachty leads Lids' new holiday campaign alongside wrestler Jade Cargill, Chase B and Eladio Carrión, built around comedy about picking gifts people actually like. It follows his September WWE appearance in Atlanta, where he lasted five minutes against Baron Corbin without being pinned.
key_facts: The Concrete x WWE collection hits Lids on November 20.
The holiday lineup also includes gear from New Era, Mitchell & Ness and '47.
Yachty's September 6 match helped Trick Williams get a title shot, and Williams won the United States Championship.
stories.why: It's a lighthearted rap-meets-wrestling crossover just in time for holiday shopping.
